In Book X of the Metamorphoses, this character is told the fate of Atalanta and Hippomenes as a warning to fear wild animals. This character is conceived after an old nurse organizes twelve nights of lovemaking between a drunk king and a young maiden. He is not Perseus, but shortly after his birth, this character is locked in a chest and given to Persephone to be fostered. The blood of this character creates the anemone flower. As an infant, he is found in the trunk of a tree, the result of his mother Myrrha's incestual affair with her father Cinyras. In most accounts, it is Artemis that sends a wild boar to gore this character to death after he is instructed to spend part of each year with his lover Aphrodite. Name this beautiful youth from Greek mythology.

This method of death claims the life of a youth who is guided to his lover each night by a light atop a tower to Aphrodite. All the citizens of a city perish in this manner after the devil tricks Dahut into stealing the key to the city gates from her father Gradlon. In Scottish legends, this method of death awaits foolish men who mount a black horse-like demon called a kelpie. Slavic folklore describes how a woman who dies in this fashion becomes a rusalka. This fate claims the lives of young English children who succumb to the sinewy arms of the grindylow, as well as Greek men who are seduced by the song of the sirens. After his wings of wax melt in the sun, Icarus dies in this manner. Identify this method of death which condemns sailors to Davy Jones's Locker.

This deity presents a stag as a gift to a young lover that accidentally spears it to death and turns into a cypress tree out of sorrow. The foundation of Apulia is attributed to a lover of this deity named Iapyx. This deity yokes a lion and a boar to a chariot in order to help a companion win his wife in marriage. A jealous love triangle involving this god and Zephyrus leads to a stray discus fatally striking the youth Hyacinthus. A lover of Cyparissus, this god becomes slave to Admetus for a year as punishment for his murder of the Cyclopes, who had earlier caused the death of this god's son Asclepius. In earlier myths, he defeats the monster Python at the site of the Oracle of Delphi. The epithet "Phoebus" is given to -- for 10 points -- what twin brother of Artemis?

This object is entrusted to a sorceress who produces a counterfeit and stages a duel between her lover and the owner of this object. A portion of it that heals wounds is thrown away as revenge for the death of Accolon. The name of this object may be related to a rainbow-producing possession of Fergus mac Roich named Caladbolg. As its owner dies, this object is ordered to be cast into a lake three times, after which a hand reaches out from the waters to grasp it. This object is first presented after a duel in which Pellinore is magically put to sleep to protect its owner. After the Battle of Camlann, Bedivere returns this object to the Lady of the Lake. It is commonly agreed that this weapon is distinct from the sword in the stone. Name this magic sword of King Arthur.

One of these entities is Vaitarna, which separates Naraka, the realm of the Hindu death deity Yama, from the earth. In Norse myth, one of these is Ifing, which separates the Jotunheim from Asgard. One myth says the son of Helios and Gaia was turned into one of these for giving water to the Titans during their battle with the Olympians; that one begins in Tartarus, and required a coin placed in the mouth of the dead to be crossed. Including Cocytus and Phegethon, FTP what mythical entities included Acheron, across which Charon ferried the dead?

One story has this deity and his consort sleeping on the thousand-headed serpent Shesha, which represents eternity. Shesha floats on a body from which the nectar of immortality, Amrita, was desired by this deity, who proceeded to churn the ocean of milk to get it. His upper-left hand holds Panchajanya, a conch shell, representing his fecundity. His consort is Lakshmi, and at certain times he can incarnate himself, as he does in the forms of Rama and Krishna. FTP what Hindu deity is the preserver?

At a sanctuary named for this goddess, Spartans would try to steal cheese while others whipped them. This goddess born on Mount Cynthus turned Arethusa [ar-uh-THOO-zuh] into a fountain in order to escape from a river god. King Oeneus forgot to make a sacrifice to this goddess, who released the Calydonian boar. This goddess killed the daughters of Niobe and transformed Actaeon into a stag. This daughter of Leto and twin sister of Apollo was often depicted as a huntress. Name this goddess whose Roman counterpart was Diana.

This god asked his daughter's suitor for alternative names to thirteen words all night until he turned to stone in daylight. This god acquired two servants after a farmer's son broke a thigh bone to get marrow. The goats Tooth-gnasher and Tooth-grinder pull this god's chariot. During a visit to Utgard, this god is unable to wrestle with old age, lift Jormungandr, or swallow the ocean. This god used a magic belt and iron gloves to defeat Geirrod, a frost giant. This father of Magni and husband of Sif owned Mjollnir, a magic hammer. Name this Norse god of thunder.

Participating in this action could turn one into a Wendigo in the myths of the Algonquin people of the Americas. Telepylus was the capital of a race of giants visited by Odysseus who engaged in this practice, the Laestrygones [les-TRIG-uh-neez]. The Thracian king Tereus unwittingly did this in a punishment crafted by his wife Procne for raping her sister Philomela. An ivory shoulder was fashioned for Pelops after Demeter unknowingly engaged in this behavior at a banquet. FTP, Tantalus was punished for allowing Demeter to violate what taboo after he cooked his son Pelops?

In the Poetic Edda, the youngest Norn is also one of these figures. The Prose Edda includes them in a list of those present at Baldur's funeral. Njal's saga describes a loom created by these figures, comprising the heads and entrails of men, a sword, and arrows. In the thirtieth stanza of Voluspa, two of these figures provide mead for Odin, while eleven others provide ale to the Einherjar. FTP, name these female warrior maidens of Norse myth, "choosers of the slain" who bring fallen fighters to Valhalla.

The Irish deity Lugh obtained one of these from the island Gorias, the possession of which guaranteed its holder couldn't lose in battle. One of these objects made from the bones of the sea monster Coinchenn was given by Scathach to an Irish hero; when that one was used in battle, its victim had to be cut open to retrieve it. That weapon, Gae Bolg, belonged to Cuchulainn. Viking warriors were alleged to throw one of these over their opponents' battle lines in order to commence battle, partly in homage to one of these weapons created by the sons of Ivaldi. FTP Odin's Gungnir is what type of weapon?

An ancient epithet for this deity is "Foremost of the Westerners," referencing his traditional realm. Certain cults worshiped this deity's soul, Banebdjedet, as a separate entity. Passion plays were re-enacted to remind his cult of his transformation during the flooding of the Nile in spring. The eldest son of Geb and Nut, his sister posthumously bore him a son, who offered his father his own eye to restore him. An oxyrhynchus fish ate the phallus of, FTP, what Egyptian deity, brother and husband of Isis?

One figure from this myth system followed a white boar into a fort where he decided to touch a golden cauldron; after doing so he was enchanted and couldn't talk or move, and later his mother was similarly caught. That figure, Pryderi, was one of seven survivors of a battle at which a giant companion was mortally wounded and asked his companions to cut off his head and return with it, where it was buried under the "white hill" facing France. Bran features prominently in this myth systems major collection, which also tells of Pwyll and Rhiannon. FTP what is this mythos recounted in the Mabinogion?

This leader first came to prominence for his attacks on the Areopagus, particularly for his prosecution and later ostracism of his rival, Cimon. As strategos, however, he was unsuccessful in campaigns against Sicyon, home of his mother Agariste. One of his many building projects was the long walls connecting his city to the port of Piraeus. His patriotic speech extolling the dead and urging his city to continue its fight against its southern rival was recorded by Thucydides as this man's "funeral oration." FTP who was this Athenian statesman at the beginning of the Peloponnesian War who initiated the building of the Parthenon?

This mythological figure was represented by the tyet, a design which represents this deity's namesake "knot" or "blood." This deity was able to make Ra reveal his secret name by fashioning a serpent from dust and Ra's spittle and then getting it to bite Ra. Knowledge of that secret name allowed this deity to stop the solar boat for help after Set, in the form of a snake, bit and poisoned the son she had hidden in a papyrus thicket. Also using her magic to refashion her husband's penis after it was eaten by a fish was, FTP, what Egyptian goddess, consort of Osiris?

This god was sometimes called Ipalnemohuani, meaning, "by whom we live." One story claims that he burned himself to death after his rival got him to drunkenly seduce a celibate priestess and subsequently became the morning star. Another story claims that he floated away on a raft of snakes. This god, said to have created mankind from the bones of previous races and blood from his penis, had a twin brother named Xolotl, and his rival was the one-footed "smoking mirror" god Tezcatlipoca. Name this "feathered serpent" god from Aztec mythology

One example of these creatures makes the sound which announces Ragnarok, after which he kills Tyr. In addition to that blood-soaked example of these creatures, Garm, these creatures include an animal which recognizes Odysseus returning home before dying, causing Odysseus to shed a tear. In addition to Argos, a more famous example of these creatures with a snake's tail is the child of Echidna and Typhon. That example of these creatures is bribed by Psyche with a cake, soothed by Orpheus's lyre, and captured by Heracles for his last labor. Name this animal, the most famous example of which is the three headed Cerberus

This figure made an otter-skin bag after killing the brother of Regin and Andvari in one story, which also sees him warn Hreidmar about a cursed ring. He distracted Svadilfari to prevent a frost giant from finishing the walls of Asgard on time in another story. That story sees this god give birth to Sleipnir while in the form of a mare. In another story Skadi set a serpent above this god after he was bound with the entrails of his son Nari for disguising himself as the giantess PÃ¶kk. This god gave a spear with mistletoe on the end of it to the blind god Hodr, leading to the death of Baldr. Name this father of Hel, Fenrir, and Jormungandr, the Norse trickster god

This deity's child with Medusa was the three-headed shepherd Cacus. This god was rescued by Thetis and Eurynome and taken to an underwater cave for nine years, until his mother saw Thetis wearing a jeweled brooch. He owns several three-legged tables with golden wheels and some gold mechanical women. This god used a thin mesh net to catch Ares cheating with his wife Aphrodite. He was found on the island of Lemnos with his legs broken after being thrown from the heavens. Name this ugly son of Hera, the Greek smith god.

In Aztec myth the underworld deity Techlotl was represented by this creature. In the Panchatantra this creature is deposed as king by the crow, which mocks him while he sleeps, leading to enmity between crows and this other bird. The demon hag Lilith is associated with this bird in Hebrew tradition. Glaucus is the name of one of these associated with the goddess for whom the Parthenon was built. FTP what are these nocturnal, predatory birds associated with Athena?

This deity posed as Vegtam, son of Valtam, in one of his travels among the dead. This god is associated with the valknut, a symbol comprising three interlaced triangles. In the Havamal, this god made a sacrifice to himself to discover the runes, and he gave his eye at Mimir's well in exchange for wisdom. This god owns an eight-legged horse whose mother was Loki in the form of a mare. This god, whose wolves are Geri and Freki, welcomes those who die in battle at Valhalla. Name this ruler of Asgard, the chief Norse god.

One of these objects, along with the Yasakani no Magatama, was hung from a tree in order to lure Amaterasu out of a cave and was known as the "eight hand" one. After losing a foot to the monster Cipactli, Tezcatlipoca replaced the foot with one of these items that emitted smoke and was made of obsidian. In order to approach and slay Medusa, Perseus used his shield as one of these items. In a fairy tale, one of these items was asked the question "Who's the fairest of them all?" by the wicked stepmother of Snow White. Name these reflective objects.

This god used a staff to prevent a rising chair from crushing him against the roof of a dwelling and then used the chair to crush Gjalp and Greip, the daughters of Geirrod. In another story, this god lost a wrestling match against the old woman Elli and failed to drain a drinking horn connected to the sea. His sons, Modi and Magni, were not the children of his golden-haired wife Sif. This god was deceived by Utgard-Loki into attempting to lift a cat that is actually his mortal enemy, the Midgard Serpent. Name this wielder of MjÃ¶lnir who was the Norse god of thunder.

This deity was raised on Rhodes by Capheira and the Telchines. After raping a Lapith woman named Caenis, this god transformed her into the male warrior Caeneus. This god found Demeter hiding in a herd of mares and fathered the talking horse Arion with her. Iphimedia's affair with this god resulted in the birth of Otus and Ephialtes. Odysseus earned this god's enmity by killing Polyphemus, this god's son. This god is also the father of the merman Triton. Name this brother of Hades and Zeus, the Greek god of the sea.

Tacitus controversially asserted that the Suebi worshipped this goddess, who was the subject of a Roman festival named for her "Navigium." In one story, she entices a snake to bite another deity in order to learn his secret name. This goddess, who is associated with the tyet symbol, travels to Byblos in order to find a box sealed within a tree. This goddess finds only thirteen of the fourteen scattered pieces of her husband's body after it is chopped up by Set. Name this Egyptian goddess, the mother of Horus and wife of Osiris.

According to Plutarch, this man died on the island of Skyros after being thrown off a cliff by Lycomedes. He is sheltered from a storm by Hecale while on his way to capture the Marathonian Bull. This man's failure to switch his black sails for white ones causes his father's suicide. He is given a sword and a ball of thread by Ariadne, who he later abandons on Naxos. He kills bandits including Procrustes while traveling to Athens, after finding his father Aegeus's sword and sandals under a rock. Name this Greek hero who slays the Minotaur.

In the Kalevala, Ilmarinen's first task in Pohjola is to plow a field infested with these animals. A creator deity who inhabits water holes is a "rainbow" type of this animal in Australian Aboriginal myth. In Hindu myth, nagas take the form of this animal. In Greek myth, Asclepius learns healing secrets from one of these animals. Two of these symmetrically appear on Hermes's staff, the caduceus, and the Ouroboros is one that eats its own tail. Name these animals which, according to another legend, were driven out of Ireland by Saint Patrick.

This deity allows Cleobis and Biton to die in their sleep, in response to their mother Cydippe's prayer for "the best gift a god can give a mortal." Sidero is murdered by Pelias atop an altar to this deity, who kills all of Lamia's children and delays Eileithyia in order to prevent Leto from giving birth. Her Homeric epithet is "boÃ´pis," or "cow-eyed." She gives Echo her namesake curse, employs Argus Panoptes to guard Io, and makes her hated stepson complete twelve labors for Eurystheus. Name this Greek goddess, the mother of Ares and wife of Zeus.

One god in this myth system, who is often depicted as a dead woman with a rope around her neck, conducts suicides to the underworld. Many deities in this people's myth system have been given somewhat generic names like "Howler Monkey God" and "God K," the latter of whom is the personification of the axe of their rain god, Chaac. One Death and Seven Death are lords of this people's underworld, Xibalba. Name this Mesoamerican people whose myths, including that of the Hero Twins Hunahpu and Xbalanque, are collected in the Popol Vuh.

Pausanias claims that this group originally consisted of three figures, including Aoide and Melete. Thamyris is blinded after losing a contest to these figures, who also judge the contest that results in Apollo's flaying of Marsyas. Depending on the source, they live on either Mount Helicon or Mount Parnassus. Among these children of Zeus and Mnemosyne are Terpsichore and Urania, who represent dance and astronomy. Clio and Calliope are members of which group of nine Greek goddesses of science, art, and literature?

One of these items belonging to Shiva is broken by Rama, winning him the right to marry Sita. Varuna gives a chariot and one of these items called Gandiva to Arjuna to use during the Kurukshetra War. One of these made of sugarcane and honeybees is owned by Kama. Penelope devises a test involving twelve axes and one of these items; after passing that test, Odysseus uses that item to kill many of her other suitors. This is the primary weapon of Philoctetes, Artemis, and Apollo. Name these weapons, with which Cupid inspires love by firing arrows.

Upon this figure's birth, this deity requested that the sixty daughters of Okeanos be made her servants, and this deity was responsible for turning Meleager's sisters to guinea fowl after their death. Brontes the Cyclops offered to make this figure anything, but this figure responded by tearing hair of his chest. One story claims that she killed another mythological figure while he was swimming away from a scorpion. One attendant of this figure, Callisto, slept with Zeus and was transformed into a bear. Oeneus forgot to offer a sacrifice to this goddess, resulting in the Calydonian Boar hunt, and a mortal who saw her bathing was eaten by his own dogs. Name this deity who turned Actaeon into a stag and wielded a silver bow, the twin sister of Apollo and Greek goddess of the moon.

In the Gaesta Denorum, this deity ordered that a golden statue of her husband be stripped down. The deity sometimes sent the handmaiden Hlin to protect selected people, while another of her attendants has a horse that can cross oceans; those figures are Gna and Hovarpnir. This goddess, the only woman who can sit on Hildskalf, is sent a linen cloak by her daughter-in-law, and on another occasion this figure was passed on to Vili and Ve, her husband's brothers. This figure, who creates the clouds from her spinning wheel, famously asked everything except for the lowly mistletoe to not harm her son, leading to Loki goading Hodr into killing that son, Baldr. Name this queen of the gods and wife of Odin.

These peoples believed that men and women were created by a war god who needed to offer human flesh to the sun to quench its hunger. That god that they worshipped lost a foot battling a crocodile in order to create the world only to replace that foot with a magic obsidian mirror. One goddess venerated by these people wore a necklace of hearts and skeletons and was impregnated by a ball of feathers. That impregnation led to a god worshipped by these people who often warred with Tezcatlipoca and is known as a "feathered serpent." which people's myth system includes Quetzalcoatl?

In Japanese myth, a pair of these creatures was the messengers of Hachiman, and after being created from flowers by Math and Gwydion, Bloddeuwed is transformed into one after betraying her husband. In Chinese myth, a group of these creatures is responsible for reuniting the cowherd and the weaver girl on the day of sevens, and in Irish mythology Dierdre has a dream about three of these animals drawing blood, foreshadowing death. In one story, after getting her tongue cut out by Tereus, Philomela and her sister Procne were turned into these creatures. Zeus transformed into one in order to kidnap Ganymede. Name this type of creature, which also includes Garuda and Crow.

He gained popularity when a cult of Khnum worshipped him, which later claimed that it was he who laid the golden cosmic egg that created the world. Some sources claim that this deity has a consort called Astennu, who stood by a lake of fire. This god's epithets include "thrice great" which led to his conflation with Hermes Trismegestus. As part of his most notable role, he was said to be the "tongue of Ra," and he once gambled with the moon to get extra light.

This figure warns his killer that he will be drowned if he is careless in crossing the sea and tells him about the island of Oskapt; that killer refuses to tell this figure his name or family. This figure wears the Helmet of Terror, owns the swords Ridill and Hrotti, and can breathe poison. His most notable possession was used to cover the dead body of his brother. To kill this figure, a hero was advised to dig more trenches so he wouldn't drown in this figure's blood; the blood running over him made him invulnerable instead and gave him the ability to understand birds. He was killed by the sword Gram, which was made by this creature's brother. This creature killed his father Hreidmar to get the gold of Andvari. Name this brother of Otter and Regin, a dragon who was killed by Sigurd in the Volsung saga.

The Megabyxus ran a cult to this deity at Ephesus, whose statues appear to have multiple rows of breasts that probably represent bull testicles or gourds. As a child, this deity pulled out Brontes' chest hair, making him appear to have mange. This deity saved Iakhos from his mother Aura, who became an insane killer as a result of insulting this deity. This deity killed the Aloadai giants by running between them, causing them to accidentally shoot one another. This deity was worshipped in a festival where young girls dressed as bears. After Oeneus failed to worship this goddess of childbirth, she sent him a beast which was killed by Atalanta and Meleager, the Calydonian Boar. Born on the floating island of Delos, this goddess turned Actaeon into a deer after he saw her bathing. Name this Greek goddess of the moon and the hunt.

This man instructed a jockey to throw down his cap at the spot where his horse stumbled; when he later ordered that spot be excavated, he discovered a pot of gold that he used to repay his master. This man tricked his rival Heinin Vardd so that he was unable to say anything other than "Blerwm, Blerwm" in front of the king. This man advised his mistress to disguise her maid as herself in order to avoid the advances of Prince Rhun. Although he is not Finn MacCool, this man gained knowledge after burning his thumb on a potion of knowledge, after which he transformed himself into a grain of wheat to evade the vengeful sorceress Ceridwen. Name this Welsh "chief of the bards" who names a Frank Lloyd Wright estate in Wisconsin.

This figure fell in love with a woman who was born with the Vedas in her memory, but she cut off her hair and lit herself on fire in response. After attempting to lift Mount Meru and disturbing Shiva and Parvati, Shiva crushed this figure's arms. He commanded all heavenly bodies to fall into place during the birth of his son, and all obeyed except Saturn; that son of this figure wielded a noose that transformed into coiling snakes and got his name from defeating a thunder god. In revenge for his sister's nose and ears being cut off, this figure was assisted by the demon Maricha in kidnapping a princess, leading to a war with the prince of Ayodhya. Name this figure usually depicted with ten heads, a Rakshasa who kidnaps Sita, the villain of the Ramayana.

This deity was so bright that soldiers could only see him from behind their shields, so the bravest warriors with the most arrow holes in their shields saw him best. This god fought the rebellion of his sister's son Copil and ordered that his heart be thrown into a lake, and this deity's attendant was Paynal. This god created the moon by killing his sister and throwing her head into the air. The Four Hundred Southerners tried to kill this wielder of the Turquoise Serpent, who was often depicted as blue. This god was born when a ball of feathers impregnated his mother Coatlicue (co-at-LI-kway). This brother of Tezcatlipoca and Quetzalcoatl helped his people settle in a place where an eagle sat on a cactus, which later became Tenochtitlan. Name this Aztec god of war and recipient of human sacrifices, who was represented as a hummingbird.

In one legend from this country, a warrior coated his arrows in his own saliva in order to slay a giant centipede. People with completely evil souls are forced to swim through river rapids filled with snakes in this country's underworld, and people who cross the river with no clothes on have their skin flayed off and hung in a tree. A "modern legend" from this country involves a woman wearing a red mask who asks people, "Am I pretty?", to which answering either "yes" or "no" will result in a gruesome death. A superstition in this country instructs people to lay out food at night or put coins in a house's foundation to please benevolent spirits. The many wild cats found in this country are said to age into massive, shapeshifting monsters called bakeneko. Name this home of yokai, also called mononoke.

A talking one of these animals was the child of Demeter while she was disguised as a Fury, although its twin Despoine was a normal goddess. Polydectes offered Perseus the task of killing Medusa as an alternative to bringing him one of these animals. After taking the form of this animal, Boreas fathered twelve of them which could run across a field of grain without crushing it; these animals were also often associated with the winds in general. Abderus is killed by some of these animals, which are defeated by being scared onto a peninsula which is cut off into an island. Hector's epithet refers to his taming of these animals. In his eighth labor, Heracles had to capture some of these animals owned by Diomedes. Name this animal, which formed the bottom half of a centaur in Greek mythology.

Herodian related how one monarch worshipped a god of this domain by walking backwards while holding the reins of an unmanned chariot during a festival. Vespasian converted Nero's massive statue to one of a god of this domain. One god of this domain was represented by a black stone taken from Emesa. A common scene in Mithraic iconography shows Mithras dining with a god of this domain atop a slaughtered bull. Marcus Aurelius Antoninus came to be known as Elagabalus due to his propitiation of a god of this domain imported from Syria. Saturnalia and a feast dedicated to a god of this domain were absorbed into Christmas in the 4th century. Aurelian propagated a cult of a god of this domain known as the "unconquered," or Invictus. Name this domain occupied by the Roman god Sol.

A first version of this object asks for one head every day but two on feast days. A crossbow, a ship, a cow, and a plow are made in the effort to create this object, but all of them are evil, so they are destroyed. This object is made of swan feathers, milk, barley, and wool. This object is the most famous creation of a figure who also creates a wife of gold and silver, since the bride he was promised in exchange for making this object rejected him. The first kantele is made from the jaw bone of a fish in order to lull the citizens of Pohjola asleep to steal this object. Louhi commissions this object, which falls into the sea when Lemminkainen and Vainamoinen fight her for it, explaining why the sea is salty. This object, forged by Ilmarinen, could produce flour, salt, and gold. Name this magical mill from the Kalevala.

In one creation myth, a male of this animal tries to name parts of a loom, only to have a female of this animal constantly veto his names. Another animal of this type traded clothes with a man named Nothing and killed him by making his stairs extra slippery. In a Choctaw myth, this animal steals fire by placing it in a clay container. One animal of this type dropped a pot full of wisdom, and a Hopi "Grandmother" of these animals creates the stars by throwing dew into the air. One animal of this kind convinced bees to fly into a jar and told a python he needed to measure him in order to tie him to a stick. That trickster figure got stuck to a tar baby he tried to fight and obtained all the stories of the world. Name these eight-legged animals including Anansi.

In one story, this deity carried off a lover and granted her dominion over flowers after diverting his brother towards carrying off Oreithyia instead. During Patroclus's funeral rites, Iris goes to this deity's house to deliver Achilles' request that this deity and his brother light the funeral pyre. This deity mated with the harpy Podarge to father the immortal horses Xanthus and Balius, and he carried Psyche to Eros's palace. This deity is often considered the most gentle of the Anemoi, and was associated with the onset of spring. Along with Poseidon and Thetis, the Argonauts made sacrifices to this deity to ensure a successful voyage. This deity flew into a jealous rage and caused a discus thrown by Apollo to hit their beloved, Hyacinthus. Name this Greek god of the west wind, brother of Notus, Eurus, and Boreas.

According to legend, one of these animals disguised himself as a deer with a firebrand tied to his tail in order to distract people and steal fire from them. After failing to carve fish out of wood, that animal caused Salmon Woman to produce salmon without her husband's knowledge. One of these animals released men from a clam shell and women from a chiton in order to let the two sexes meet for the first time, and he is later swallowed by a whale. In alternate myths, one of these animals either turns into a clump of dirt in a woman's drinking water to be reborn as a fussy baby or stabs a seagull with a thorn in order to release the sun, moon, and stars. The Morrigan takes the form of one of these birds, and Huginn and Muninn are two of these birds which report news to Odin. Name this animal, a non-Coyote Native American trickster figure.

One priest of this god, Pra'em-hab, complained about being taxed more than other gods' priests. Seventy-two conspirators including Queen Aso helped this god, whose army was destroyed when his enemy turned into a giant disk and blinded them. In one myth, this god is kept chained in the Great Bear by Taweret; this god ripped himself from his mother's womb since he was too impatient to be born normally. This god was associated with the carp, which ate the penis of a man he had ripped apart. This god of foreigners was tricked into eating lettuce with some semen on it, as well as losing a boat race because he made a boat of stone which sank. This husband of Nephythys (Nef-this) fought Apep on Ra's boat and battled with Horus, who was trying to avenge his father. Name this god of storms who killed his brother Osiris.

In German folklore, Hettel's servant Wade uses one of these objects to abduct Hilde; that object is thus colloquially synonymous with trickery. Sergestus destroys one of these objects and is beaten by Cloanthus in the first event at Anchises' funeral games. The dwarf Litr is burned in flames that appear when Hyrrokkin violently moves one of these objects at Baldr's funeral. Skidbladnir was a foldable one of these objects, while Naglfar is one made entirely of fingernails. A talking piece of timber from the forest of Dodona is part of one of these objects; in an epic named after that object, a group of heroes escapes the Clashing Rocks and journeys to Colchis for the Golden Fleece on this object. Name these objects, examples of which include the Argo.

In Japanese folklore, a girl from Matsuyama communes with her dead mother via one of these objects, which causes her stepmother to suspect her of witchcraft. It's not an eye, but in one legend, Tsukuyomi was born from one of these things. In Greek myth, the Furies constantly show one of these objects to Orestes as they follow him. One of these objects is hung from a tree along with jewels and white clothes after roosters crow and a goddess makes the other gods laugh with a lewd dance. After his foot was eaten by Cipactli, one god replaced his foot with an obsidian one of these items. Amaterasu was lured out of her cave by one of these objects placed by its entrance, and Tezcatlipoca was named after a "smoking" variety of this object. To avoid looking at the head of Medusa, Perseus used Athena's shield as, what kind of reflective object?

The process of this action being done to the Roman Empire was initiated by the city of Smyrna. That instance of this type of event was predicted by the daughter of Cheiron. This happened to one man who rescued his sister Renpetneferet from Djoser, and who helped end a seven-year famine. This happened to one man who angered Zeus by using Medusa's blood, and whose children included Aglaea, Iaso, and Aceso. Seneca the Younger ridiculed this process in a work titled for the "Pumpkinification" of one man who underwent it. Cadmus's daughters Ino and Semele underwent this process, after which they were known as Thyone and Leucothea. Give this process which Romulus underwent to become Quirinus, which was also done to Roman emperors after they died, beginning with Julius Caesar.

This god attempted to kick Chaya, one of his father's maids, but instead she cursed him and his leg became infested with maggots. In one myth, this deity's son refuses to ascend to heaven because he does not want to leave behind a companion he has had since leaving Hastinapura, a small dog. This deity had transformed into that dog in order to test Yudhishthira's righteousness. This god known as "shrivelled foot" threw a noose to capture Markandeya's soul, but failed because he was kicked to death by an infuriated Shiva. This father of the oldest Pandava is the son of Saranya and the sun god Surya. He is aided by Agni, who brings people to his realm, Chitragupta. He records the good and evil actions of every human being, and he sits in judgment at Naraka. Name this first mortal to die, the Hindu god of death.

This fate happened to Mestra's father, whom Demeter had punished for cutting down a sacred grove; Demeter sent Limos to punish him, forcing Erysichthon to do this action to himself. This thing happened to Abderus while he was assisting Hercules during his eighth labor, and in revenge, Hercules caused this thing to happen to the giant king of Thrace. This was the method of death of travelers who were forced by Sciron to wash his feet and in one case, this was done to a rock instead of its intended target due to a trick by Rhea. It's not being turned into an animal, but Artemis caused this thing to happen to Actaeon after he stumbled on her naked in the forest, and the mares of Diomedes would often do this thing to people. Name this thing which happened to the children of Kronos.

In the Gylfaginnig, one of these beings was said to have been born from yeast-drops when the breath of heat met the rime. Two of these creatures are tied to a millstone and sing the pirate Mysing into existence as revenge. One of these beings pretends that three hammer-blows felt like acorns falling on his head, but actually dodged them, letting them create craters where they landed. After refusing to let an ox cook, then eating all of it, one of these beings is hit by a pole which adheres to it, allowing it to fly away in the form of an eagle. One of these beings sweated a male and female out of its armpits and feeds on the milk of Audumbla, while another kidnapped Loki to steal the apples of Idun. Thiazi and Ymir are two of these beings, which fight the gods at Ragnarok. Name these Norse creatures, also known as jotunn.

In one myth, two girls refuse to go to this figure because they can still see their sewing needles, so a third girl is sent to get a light from this figure and is made to sort dirt from poppy seeds before receiving a skull on a stick. This figure orders a boy to carry water in a sieve to fill a tub, and a black cat advises the boy and his sister to throw a towel and comb behind them to escape this figure. This figure, who commands white, red, and black horsemen, gives aid to Vasilisa the Fair. The house of this figure constantly turns to face away from visitors, as depicted by Viktor Hartmann. This figure sweeps away all traces of herself with a silver broom. Name this crone who flies around in a mortar and pestle and lives in a hut with chicken's legs from Slavic mythology.

These animals were the symbols of the god of the Memphite necropolis titled "He of tomb entrances" who was often syncretised with Osiris and Ptah. These animals symbolized a son of Horus who was under the protection of Serket. One of these creatures known as "He Who Came Into Being By Himself," and helped Atum create the earth. Seker and Qebehsenuef were both associated with these animals, and the "Bennu" one represented Ra's soul. Egyptians believed that the spiritual aspect of the soul which survived beyond death took the form of one of these creatures, known as the ba. Both of Hathor's consorts had the head of one of these creatures, and a deity with the head of one of these creatures tricked a rival into eating lettuce spread with his semen, avenging the murder of his father, Osiris. Name this animal associated with Horus.

A Ute myth describes how the enraged hare-god Ta-wats attacked a god of this thing after that god, Ta-va, injured his shoulder, and the Mongolians believed that the marmot was created after another hero claimed he would cut off his thumbs and live in a hole if he failed in his assault against seven of these things. Another myth claims that these things were the children of Xi He and Di Jun, and were shot down by the archer Hou Yi. That was because nine of these things had come out simultaneously, not successively. In another myth, the goddess Uzume performed a comical strip tease which made the gods laugh so hard that the goddess of this object decided to emerge from the cave she had been hiding in because her brother Susanoo killed one of her attendants. Name this domain of the goddess Amaterasu, whose brother Tsukuyomi was god of the moon.

The Kshir Sagar was composed entirely of this substance, and, along with Vaikuntha, serves as a residence of Vishnu. According to the Matsya Purana, a wife of Brahma named Surabhi first produced this substance. The demoness Putana tried to kill Krishna by offering him this substance. The Halahala poison was swallowed by Shiva after it originated from this substance, on which the serpent Adisesha rests. Vishnu's sixth avatar, Parasurama, went on a Kshatriya genocide when Kartavirya stole a wish-granting creature that also produced this substance; those creatures were also tended by gopis like Radha. Mount Mandar was placed in this substance to produce amrit, and the naga Vasuki served as a rope in order to "churn" an ocean of it. Identify this substance produced by Kamadhenu, the first cow.

A prophecy about this figure describes his first two trips to Hatti as good, but the third as a disaster. This god is granted power in a ceremony in which he makes cloth vanish and reappear. He is known as the "Quickener of the Death" and "Pure Incantation," as well as Asari, and he leads the Three Hundred Igigi. During the New Year, a statue of this god's son was moved to his cult center so the two could talk; he later gave that son the mushussu dragon. This god, who rides four horses with poison in their mouths, was worshipped at Esagila and Etemenanki. This consort of Sarpanitu used wind to inflate the body of an enemy before shooting her with arrows. This god with fifty names then defeats Kingu to gain the Tablets of Destiny. Name this Babylonian deity who killed Tiamat to become ruler of the gods.

This deity orders gold stripped from a statue for personal adornment and presides over Var, guardian of promises, and Syn, who locks doors in halls. This deity intercedes on behalf of the childless king Rerir, and she sends a maid to warn Geirrod about a stranger whom no dogs would attack. This child of Fjorgynn defends a god accused of knocking at doors as a fortuneteller in the Lokasenna, only to be accused of sleeping with her husband's brothers as a result. This goddess has handmaidens named Lofn, Hlin, Gna, and Fulla, and she is able to weave clouds. She ignores an object she thinks is unthreatening while travelling and asking every other object not to harm her son. Loki then exploits her mistake by fashioning a weapon made from mistletoe. Name this Norse goddess of wisdom, marriage, and love, the mother of Baldr and wife of Odin.

In one story, this figure makes a medicine for Erec, and a text purportedly written by this self-declared "governor of the waves" relates the tale of Piers the Fierce. This figure, who taught mathematics to Moronoe, Mazoe, and Thiten, fights for the attentions of Hector de Maris and Berengier against Sebile. By creating a golden ship, this figure causes a man to interfere in the feud of Damas and Ontzlake. The maid Rocedon helps a man escape from this figure, who traps him in Cart Castle until he chooses between her and two other women. This figure feuds with a woman who caught her having an affair with Guiomar, and she tricks Accolon into fighting his ruler with his own sword. This wife of King Urien and sister of Morgause transports her brother to Avalon after his death. Name this enchantress, the enemy and half-sister of King Arthur.

The necklace of Harmonia was made from the hair of these figures, one of whom turned into an owl until Zeus fell asleep before appearing in the form of a beast to Dionysus. The Harpies took the daughters of King Pandareus to be servants to these figures. In the Aeneid, one of these figures turns into a small bird and flies in the face of Turnus during battle, while another implants a snake in Amata's chest to drive her insane. Oedipus dies in a grove sacred to these beings. They're not the Meliae, but these figures emerged from Uranus's blood falling on the earth, not the sea. Dido called on these figures when she was on her funeral pyre, and examples of these figures include Alecto, Megaera, and Tisiphone. These figures were ironically called the "kindly ones," or the Eumenides. Name these goddesses of vengeance, especially for the murder of a parent..

Jane Harrison's Prolegomena to the Study of Greek Religion controversially argues that one member of this group was a divine being when depicted with a prophylatic mask. A minor Argonaut of the name Mopsus was killed by a snake that was created when the blood of one member of this group was mixed with sand from the Libyan Desert. Born under Mount Olympus, one myth relates that the Atlas mountains were formed when Heracles gave the remains of one of them to Atlas. When one of them died, both Chrysaor and Pegasus was born from that member of this group's blood. The hero who encountered this group learned their location from figures that shared only one tooth and one eye. King Polydectes assigned that hero to find one of them. Two of them, named Stheno and Euryale, are immortal. Name these figures that include a figure whose gaze can petrify, Medusa.

According to Snorri, a creature filled with the lifeblood of all men that die will consume this location and use its remains to smear the sky. Two figures carrying the Simul are transported to this location in a different story. Alternately, those figures, Hjuki and Bil, are said to affect this location's inhabitability. In Greek myth, the deity associated with this location was enraptured by a king of Elis while he was asleep. That deity of this location is the offspring of Pallas and is the sibling of Eos, Rosy-Fingered Dawn. Ragnarok will begin when the wolf Hati devours the entirety of this object. Identify this location represented by the Norse goddess Mani, a celestial object also represented by the Greek figures Selene and Artemis.

The penultimate chapter of From Ritual to Romance offers the thesis that the frequent occurrence of this word is inspired by the heretical nature of Holy Grail legends. This word also appears in the name of a location that King Arthur passed through while enchanted by Annowre. In one story, a place described by this word is built by Queen Brangamore. In that story, that place is connected to a task that involves fighting a floating hand, a floating head, and the Devil. At another place described by this adjective, Lancelot cuts a piece of cloth from a dead knight the moment he feels a tremor. In addition to naming that aforementioned chapel, this adjective also describes a certain location occupied by Galahad, who first did so while he was so "tender of age." identify this adjective that describes a seat of the Round Table that gets its name because most people who sit in it will die.

A fragmentary text describes this mythological figure near the sea coast running toward a tree that has diamonds and crystals Â– which may be antimony Â– growing on it. This hero encounters two scorpion men at a mountain before crossing under that mountain for ten days. He then has a long conversation with an alewife about crossing the waters of death. Near the end of one work in which this figure appears, a plant belonging to this hero is devoured by a snake, which subsequently sheds its skin. This hero was not able to stay awake for seven days, as evidenced by a certain figure baking bread daily for him, so that when this character awakes, he can observe the rotting. Earlier, this man and his friend had travelled to Cedar Forest to kill a monster sacred to Enlil. Identify this king that is the slayer of Humbaba, the namesake of an ancient Mesopatamian epic.

This god is depicted breathing fire from his mouth, standing atop a reptilian, and burning it in a seminal image in the Codex Vaticanus. In some depictions, this god wields an axe shaped like a dragon. He also is depicted with a blue ribbon over his mouth. A statue of this god supposedly can be found east of Tezcuco inside a mountain made entirely of solid white lava. He's not associated with war, but that mountain honors this figure's association with the west. This figure was responsible for smiting the earth with fire, ending the Third Sun. This figure fathered the moon god Teccizetecatl. He married "she of the jade skirt," Chalchiuhtlicue, after Tezcatlipoca took this figure's first wife. This god is an analogue of the Mayan god Chac. Identify this husband of Xochiquetzal, the Aztec god of rain and water, who also received numerous human sacrifices.

This man refused to divulge the burial location of Neleus to King Nestor, and one account of his demise relates that he, too, was a robber slain by Theseus. This figure struck a deal with another man to make the spring Peirene flow behind a temple of Aphrodite. That occurred in a city that this man founded, which is sometimes called Ephyra, and was supposedly populated with men that sprung from mushrooms. This figure started the Isthmian Games and had earlier used the letters "SS" to brand the feet of cattle that did not belong to Autolycus, thus proving Autolycus a thief. He was punished for revealing the divine secrets of Zeus to Asopus, and later he tricked Hades by demonstrating to him the use of handcuffs. He also tricked Persephone into going back to the world above temporarily, after which this figure was punished eternally. Name this resident of Hades charged with endlessly rolling a boulder.

Inscriptions found in Sarmizegetusa and Aachen syncretize the rejuvenating powers of Grannus with the Roman form of this figure. He supposedly liked to spend time at Patara during the winter, where a female oracle honored him. This figure was angered when his lover Carnus was killed for his prophetic powers. He's not Eros, but Homer relates that this deity had arrows of gold that could drive away the clouds. He eloped with Creusa to Libya, and there he founded the city of Cyrene. This figure is the father of the apiculturist Aristaeus. Tmolus awarded this figure a prize for besting another figure. In another instance, he flayed the skin of his opponent, Marsyas. This man was also the dedicatee of a series of games held in Pythia at his namesake temple, where he killed the Python. Name this Greek god of light, music and poetry.

Pausanias recorded that nearby this location is a town whose residents received an oracle that they would all perish when sunlight made contact with the bones of Orpheus. That prophecy is inspired by the fact that Leibethra, where Orpheus is buried, is near this location. Another story claims that after the mares of Diomedes were retrieved by Heracles, Eurystheus set them free, and they came to this place. The primordial figure Euryonome was viciously assaulted by Ophion before being driven from this location, whose inhabitants were attacked by the conniving Otus and Ephilates. Almost every resident of this place possess bodies filled with the substance ichor. The gigantomachy and the titanomachy were revolts against the denizens of this place, whose members include Hebe and Ganymede. Identify this mythological mountain home to Hestia and Zeus.

Stages of this event include a crowd of people crossing over a bridge and getting insults hurled at them by masked men, as well taking a pig from the city to the sea, washing and sacrificing it. This event, which also involves drinking a mixture of mead, water, and pennyroyal known as kykeon, partially takes place in a massive underground chamber where two priestesses, wrapped in darkness, speak to a crowd. Other portions of this event see a dance on the Rharian Fields, and this tradition was initiated after Demophoon was nearly made immortal. This set of practices is split into Lesser and Greater portions, of which we know nothing about the latter, except that it honors Kore and Doso. Name this set of actions that allows one to join the cult of Demeter, named for a city in Attica.

In this work, a hero's mother asks the question "Name the first of the destroyers," to which her son responds with "eagle," before he notes that he has a magic potion that defends against eagles. In one section of this work, its main character seeks out magical incantations from a wise man, only to learn that they are in his stomach. This work also recounts the morphing of cows into bears, causing the death of the person milking those cows, which is told to detail the angst one figure has for his owner Untamo. Another section of this book describes the formation of a zither-like instrument called the kantele, which the protagonist plays. Other figures in this work include Louhi, the Maid of Pohjola, as well as the forger of the Sampo. Identify this work compiled by Elias Lonrott, the national epic of the Finns.

On a notable horologium a representation of this god is situated between a god called Lips and a god called Skiron. In some stories, the wife of this god is a nymph of Elysium. This god is the father of Carpus with his wife, who possesses eternal dominion over flowers. He is not Zeus, but this god's offspring includes a pair of immortal animals that Peleus gave to his son. In addition to fathering Achilles's horses Xanthus and Balius with the harpy Podarge, this god accidentally killed a Spartan prince while he played a game with his lover. In another story, he takes away Psyche to a beautiful valley after Psyche's parents consult an oracle. This god was responsible for the aforementioned death of Apollo's lover Hyacinthus when he redirected a discus. Name this brother of Notus and Boreas, the Greek personification of the West Wind.

In the Aeneid, Pallas throws a spear through the chest of this man's son, Halaesus. This mythological figure slew Tantalus, king of Pisa, and took his wife, arousing the ire of the Dioscuri. After killing a deer on Mount Icarion, this man boasted that "Not even Artemis" could have made such a shot. This killer of Antiphus spent his early life in the court of Tyndareus and later, his wife would urge him to walk down a red carpet. He took Cassandra as a concubine after the Trojan War, which he began by attempting to appease Artemis by sacrificing his daughter, Iphigeneia. Upon returning to Mycenae, this son of Atreus was killed by Aegisthus and his wife, Clytemnestra. Name this brother of Menealus, the high king of the Greeks during the Trojan War.

One of these figures was a physician, who fought against Vidyunmali and was the son of Yama, Sushena. Sushena was the father of another of these figures, who some myths claimed to be one of the Apsara, and helped to appease Lakshmana. That figure, Tara, was married to another one of these creatures, who fathered Angada and battled with Mayavi before being killed by his brother. A group of these creatures lived in a place called Kishkinda in the Dandaka Forest and were called the Vanaras. One of the members of that group was a son of Surya, who married Ruma and commanded a legion of these animals, Sugriva. Another one of these creatures was the son of Vayu, who helped to build a bridge in order to save Sita from Ravana in the Ramayana. Name these creatures from Hindu mythology as exemplified by Hanuman.

A collection of myths titled for this figure "Travelling" was transcribed by John Swanton from the narration of Skaay. This figure once stole a hat from the Fog Man, after which he made his way to the Man Who Sits On The Tides and convinced him to stand up and stretch twice a day. In another story, this figure pried a bunch of chitons off the side of a rock, freeing a group of women that he then introduced to the men he'd released from a clam shell. In a third story, he seduced a rival's daughter, allowing him access to a longhouse containing the Sun, the Moon, the stars, and fresh water, which he stole and released to the world. From that rival, Gray Eagle, he also stole a brand of fire, the smoke from which permanently changed his outer coloring. Identify this trickster god of various Northwestern Native American myth systems who is not to be confused with his cousin Crow.

The Narmer Palette depicts the sistrum-bearing deity as one of these creatures. In Zoroastrianism, the Vendidad declares the urine of this animal to be cure for all illnesses. In Hinduism, Kamadhenu was one of these animals and Prithu was able to plant crops after catching the goddess Prithvi in the form of one of the creatures. In Egyptian mythology, Anubis was believed to be the son of one of these animals, who was often depicted as carrying a tray of food. In addition to Hesat, another of these creatures created Buri and nourished itself by licking the salt blocks of Ginnungagap, Audhumla. Odysseus' crewman got into some serious trouble for eating these animals that belong to Helios and Pasiphae dressed up as one of these in order to seduce the father of Minotaur. Io was turned into, what type of animal, which are extremely sacred to Hindus.

This figure supposedly rose to fame after defeating a pair of violent Siamese twins, the Moloindes, who were employed by the Eleans to attack this man's city. Some accounts state that this man's good fortune was an attempt by Apollo to atone for the murder of Niobe's children. While he was away in Gerenia, this man's father, his brothers, Pero and Alastor were butchered by Heracles for refusing to purify him. This son of Neleus convinced his superior to present gifts including the seven tripods and nearly died after his chariot's horses were shot by Paris. This man's son, Anitlochus, finished second in the chariot race and third in the foot race at Patroclus' funeral games. This man reconciled Achilles and Agamemnon, and at the advice of Mentor, Telemachus visited his palace at Pylos in the Odyssey. Name this figure respected as one of the oldest and wisest Greeks during the Trojan War.

This deity was sometimes combined with the goddess of the dead Amentet to become the solar goddess of the west. This goddess was associated with protective eye of the primordial snake, Wadjet, as well as a piece of jewelry known as the menat. Â Sharing her most distinctive feature with the predynastic goddess Bat, this deity, who had a major cult center at Dendara was closely associated with the sycamore. The sistrum was dear to this mother of Harsomtus, who poured milk over her husband's eyes to heal them after Set plucked them out. As the Eye of Re, this wife of Horus became wrathful and her slaughtering spree only ended when she was tricked into drinking beer from the Nile. Name this Egyptian goddess who sometimes takes on the destructive form of Sekhment but is usually the calm cow-headed goddess of love and fertility.

The waterfall, Assaroe, was named for one of these figures who happened to drown in said waterfall and another with the sobriquet "the Red" married Maga. Another of these figures became a stammerer after being wounded in battle by a spear. The daughter of one of these figures was raised by twelve foster-fathers and became pregnant after drinking from river with two worms in it. That daughter fell in love with another one of these figures, who needed seven women to please him and had his sword stolen from him while having sex with a woman who could be pleased by thirty women. That man also cut off the tops of three hills after being replaced in this role by a seven year old, who was unable to fight during a venture to seize Donn Culainge led by Aillil and Medb. That man was preceded in this role by Fergus Mac Roich and saw Naoise elope with his lover in waiting, Deidre. Conchobar Mac Nessa held, what position that ruled over Cuchulainn's hometown.

This man received a prophesy about Amphritite unyolking Poseidon's chariot from three goat-skin wearing women known as the Timeroi at Lake Tritonis. This man prophesied that the creation of island of Calliste to Euphemus. This figure, who was responsible for taming the two automatons known as Chalkotauroi, fathered the twins, Euneus and Nebrophonus, on the island of Lemnos with Hypsipyle. In some myths, this man was eaten by a dragon, whom he later slayed. This figure then created the Sparti from the teeth of that dragon, which he sowed into a field. He would later marry a figure known as either Creusa or Glauce, who would be killed by this figure's former lover. This man, who lost a sandal in the Anauros, was accompanied by men like Calais and Zetes on his most famous task, which was commissioned by King Pelias and forced this man to travel to Colchis. Name this man, the lover of Medea, who went on a quest for the Golden Fleece with his Argonauts.

According to Pausanias, this figure was identified in many places with Hemera and this deity allegedly had a dalliance with the son of Mantius, Cleitus. Children of this equivalent to the Etruscan Thesan include Pyroeis and Phainon. According to another account, this deity abducted the lover of the daughter of Erectheus, an Athenian youth named Cephalus and with Astraeus, this goddess bore the four winds. Because she was caught once with Ares, Â Aphrodite cursed her, causing her to marry the father of Emathion and Memnon. For that lover, this figure obtained immortality but not eternal youth, causing Tithonus to become so old that he eventually turned into a cicada. FTP, name this rosy-fingered, saffron-robed figure from Greek mythology, the herald of her brother Helios, and the personification of dawn.

St. Boniface is believed to have cut down an oak tree dedicated to this deity and this god was invoked by the Kvinneby amulet. This god tricked a figure who would later be turned into stone into marrying his daughter and at another event, the servant Beyla announces this figure's arrival. One of this god's stepsons was invoked in duels and was renowned for his attractiveness and skiing abilities. This stepfather of Ullr used Himinbjotr or Sky-Bellower as bait while fishing with the husband of Hrodr, Hymir. This deity once dressed as a bride in order to exact revenge on the giant, Thyrm, and also provided the giant cauldron for feast of Aegir. This resident of Bilskirnir killed the giant, Hrungnir, after Hrungir claimed that he would destroy Valhalla and abduct Freya and this man's wife, Sif. Goats pull the chariot of, what owner of Meginjord and Mjolnir, the Norse god of thunder.

The story of this man appears in Lucian's "On the Syrian Goddess," a text that claims that he built a temple to Atargatis possibly found at Hierapolis. Â This man's children include Hellen and Protogenea. Â This man's most notable action was precipitated by Lycaon's sacrifice of a young boy and by Lycaon's sons serving the organs of their murdered brother Nyctimus in a stew. Â Sharing his name with a king of Crete who fathered Idomeneus, this son of Prometheus refused to allow animals into a chest that he crafted. Â name this figure from Greek mythology who survived a flood alongside his wife, Pyrrha.

The ability of this man and his sons to stop the flow of blood from a wound by saying a spell is one of the few instances of magic appearing in the works of Homer. Â That episode occurs after this man's descendants participate in a hunt for a boar that resides in a thicket so dense that it is completely dark. Â One crime committed by this man led Eurytus to detest Heracles, and, after Iphitus attempted to right that crime, Iphitus was killed by Heracles in a fit of madness. Â In one story, his touch is able to impart the quality of invisibility, while in another story he steals some cattle from Euboea. One of the opponents of Krishna, a demon named Keshi, takes the form of this animal that is at the center of the Asvamedha Sacrifice. Â One of these animals with seven heads emerged during the churning of the ocean and is called Uchaishravas. Â In the Ulster Cycle, two of these animals emerge from the waters of Linn Liath and are named after their grey and black color. Â One of these animals helps a mason build the walls of Asgard and is named Svadilfari, while other examples of these animals from Norse myth include the aspects of day and night, Skinfaxi and HrÃ-nfaxi. Â The water dwelling Kelpie resembles this animal, one group of which kills Abderus during the eighth labor of Heracles and belongs to Diomedes. Â name these animals exemplified by the eight legged Sleipnir.

One ruler of this location was helped by a group of fish that rose up from the sea to carry her expedition of boats to invade a neighboring region. Â Another ruler of this location came to power by killing a usurper of his elder brother's throne. Â The father of the first ruler of this location was born in a hut that was thatched with cormorant feathers, and amongst the ancestors of that first ruler of this place were Heaven's-Sun-Height and Luxuriant-Jewel-Princess. Â The first ruler of this location was advised by a three-legged crow, and he conquered it by realizing that he had to attack from the east. Â Mythological rulers of this place, including Suizei and Jimmu, are documented in the Nihongi and the Kojiki. Â name this place created as the children of Izanami and Izanagi, an Asian archipelago.

In one story, the prince Senopati had a three day long sexual encounter with one of these figures, after which he founded the Mataram kingdom in Cambodia. Â The boy Astika prevented Janamejaya from executing a planned genocide of these figures, one of whom murdered Parikshit by poisoning his food. Â One of these figures loved to meditate and asked for power over his own mind from the gods, and he was tasked with supporting the world. This figure acquired the Sword of David while sailing on Solomon's ship and Evelake crafted this figure's shield, which featured a red cross of blood drawn by Joseph of Arimethea. This figure's grandfather sought out Dame Brusen to acquire a ring that would make his daughter look like the lover of this man's father. This grandson of Pelles saved a duke's daughter by defeating seven knights at the Castle of Maidens and had been raised by his great aunt in a nunnery. Merlin died when he tried to sit in Siege Perilous, the seat reserved for this son of Elaine at the Round Table and he proved himself to King Arthur when he removed a sword from a piece of marble in a river. One of three men to see the Holy Grail along with Bors and Perceival, name this "Perfect Knight", the illegitimate son of Lancelot.

The atheist Diagoras was said to have pointed out that people who died in events of this sort did not leave offerings in temples. Nauplius got revenge on Agamemnon by causing many of these events near Euboea. After surviving one of these events, Ajax the Lesser died when a god split a rock he was resting on. Zeus killed a man on the way to the Oracle of Delphi in one of these events because he had called his wife "Hera"; after the death of that man, Ceyx, his wife Alcyone killed herself and became a kingfisher. All but one of a certain group are killed in this sort of event after they ignore Tiresias's warnings and eat the cattle of Helios. After becoming the only survivor of one of these events, Odyssey arrives at Ogygia, Calypso's island. The Sirens caused what sorts of accidents by luring boats to their rocky island?

To imprison Llao, the Klamath god of hell, the sky god Skell creates one of these natural features from the lava of Mount Mazama. It's not a cave, but Percival uses an adder stone to kill the invisible Afanc monster, which terrorizes one of these natural features. The Ojibwe believe that the copper near one of these features is guarded by Mishipeshu, a scaly horned panther. After her birth from Pallas, Athena was raised near one of these natural features named for Triton. After she causes the execution of his mother, Sir Balin the Savage beheads a spirit from one of these features. This sort of feature provides the name of a woman who enchanted Merlin and raised Lancelot near one of these places. The woman who gives Excalibur to King Arthur is known as the "Lady" of what sort of body of water?

Two of this deity's sons, Polygonus and Telegonus, were defeated by Heracles after they were sent to challenge him by Hera. According to Virgil, this god explained that the sickness of some bees was punishment for the death of Eurydice when he was visited by Aristaeus. In Book 8 of the Metamorphoses, Achelous compares this god to Erysichthon's daughter Mestra, who shared his best-known ability. This deity's daughter Eidothea advised a hero and his men to capture this god by hiding under some skins. According to Homer, this deity's home was at Pharos, where he once disguised himself as one of its sea lions. This deity was forced to divulge information about the future to Menelaus after being captured. Name this shape-shifting Greek deity, the so-called "Old Man of the Sea."

An artifact from this city may have represented the southern stars through a goddess's headdress of marigolds, and was found in a structure in this city that emulated a mythological "Serpent Mountain." After a snake goddess's son led a rebellion during an idol procession of this city's patron god, his heart was thrown to the spot where this city was founded. A stone at the base of a temple in this city depicts the dismemberment of a moon goddess who led her 400 brothers to decapitate their mother. A blue water pot found in this city was dedicated to a rain god who, after his first wife was kidnapped by a night god, married a jade-skirted goddess. Half of the Templo Mayor in this city was dedicated to a "left-handed hummingbird" god. Name this city founded where a snake-eating eagle was perched on a cactus, the Aztec capital.

It's not the Sphinx, but the Naxians of Delos built a terrace of marble statues of this animal dedicated to Apollo. The Speos Artemidos temples were built for a goddess of this form whose names means "she who tears," Pakhet. Two of these animals look away from each other in a symbol of the earth deity Aker. Ptah's wives and his son, the war god Maahes, were depicted with the head of this animal. The "destructive eye of Ra" took the form of this animal when she ran amok on the Earth, but was pacified after she mistook pomegranate alcohol for blood. This was the animal form of Hathor's violent counterpart, Sekhmet. For his first labor, Heracles strangled one of these animals. Name these animals, one of which with impenetrable fur lived in Nemea.

The name "Pārvati" means "daughter of" these beings, whose king was her father Himāvat. While he is flying to Lanka, Hanumān encounters one of these beings named Mainak, the only one that did not have its wings severed by Indra. Having failed to find the Sanjīvani herb that could heal Lakshmana, Hanumān returns to the battlefield after picking up one of these objects. To protect the residents of Gokul from the storms of Indra, Krishna lifts one of these objects with his pinky. During the churning of the milky ocean, the serpent Vāsuki was wrapped around one of these landforms. Shiva lives on the largest one of these landforms, Kailash. Name these natural features, the holiest of which is Meru.
